name: CAKE
description: Over the past few years, emotion recognition in adults has been a topic of interest in the research community as the majority of publicly available datasets contains more adults, leaving emotion recognition in children underexplored. Recognizing children’s emotional states poses extra challenges due to morphological variations and less developed cognitive abilities, contributing to different expression patterns compared to grown-up individuals. Thus, current state-of-the-art models trained on adult emotions often struggle to perform effectively when applied to children. To address these gaps, we introduce a novel context-aware kid emotion in-the-wild dataset (CAKE) that features children between 4 and 12 years old derived from movies. The dataset contains 259 audio-visual clips in natural social scenarios labeled with diverse and rich emotion annotations, including 12 different emotional states, valence and arousal, as well as text-based context reasoning. Furthermore, we conduct benchmark experiments with transfer learning on existing adult and child datasets. Experimental results show a promising performance on our proposed dataset with room for improvement, which will serve as a solid benchmark for future research on child emotion recognition.
